??? question "What do we call a variable declared with `let` inside a function?"

    A local variable. It needs an initializer and is visible from its declaration to the end of its block.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#35-local-variable-declarations).

??? question "What is text for human readers that the compiler skips called, and how is it written in v0.1?"

    A comment. It starts with `//` and runs to the end of the line; block comments are not part of v0.1.

    Introduced in [2. Basic source rules](02-basic-source-rules.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../specification/lexical-structure.md#22-comments).

??? question "Which v0.1 type holds a fixed number of values of one type, with sizes known at compile time, such as `[f32; 4]`?"

    A fixed-size array. Its element type and every dimension are part of its type.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#71-array-types).

??? question "Which return type means a function hands back no value, and may be left out?"

    The type `void`. It describes the absence of a value, so it cannot be stored in a variable.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#42-primitive-types).

??? question "Inside a string or character literal, what do we call `\n` or `\t`?"

    An escape sequence, a backslash and a character that stand for something hard to type. v0.1 supports `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"` and `\'`.

    Introduced in [2. Basic source rules](02-basic-source-rules.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../specification/lexical-structure.md#character-and-string-literals).

??? question "What tells the compiler what kind of value something is and what can be done with it?"

    Its type. Every Vortex expression has exactly one type, known before the program runs.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md).

??? question "In `let height: usize = 64;`, what is the `: usize` part called, and when may you leave it out?"

    A type annotation. You may leave it out of a local variable declaration when the type can be inferred from the initializer.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md).

??? question "What is it called when the compiler works out a local variable's type from its starting value?"

    Type inference. Vortex does it only for local variables, and the inferred type is still fixed before the program runs.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#410-type-inference).

??? question "What do we call the list of an array's sizes, one per dimension?"

    Its shape. For `[f32; 2, 3]` the shape is `[2, 3]`, and it is part of the type.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#75-rank-and-shape).

??? question "What do we call a variable that is allowed to change after it is created, and how do you declare one?"

    Mutable. You declare it with `let mut`; a variable without `mut` is immutable.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [9. References and mutability](../specification/references.md#93-local-mutability).

??? question "How can a function read or change an existing value without copying it, and how are the two kinds written?"

    Through a reference. `&T` is a shared reference for reading; `&mut T` is a mutable reference that can also change the value.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [9. References and mutability](../specification/references.md#91-reference-types).

??? question "When nothing around it asks for another type, what type does a whole-number literal get, and a decimal one?"

    Their default types, `i32` for a whole number and `f32` for a decimal.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#43-integers).

??? question "In `[f32; 4]`, what is `f32` called?"

    The element type, the single type shared by every element of the array.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#71-array-types).

??? question "What do we call a language in which every value has a type known before the program runs?"

    Statically typed. Vortex is statically typed, even when a local variable's type is inferred.

    Introduced in [1. Syntax philosophy](01-syntax-philosophy.md).

??? question "What kind of type is built into the language and named by a keyword, such as `i32` or `bool`?"

    A primitive type. v0.1 has `void`, `bool`, `char`, `i32`, `u32`, `usize`, `f32`, `f64` and `String`.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#42-primitive-types).

??? question "In `let width = 128;`, what is the expression after `=` called?"

    The initializer. It gives the variable its first value and, if no type is written, its type; v0.1 requires one.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#35-local-variable-declarations).

??? question "What kind of type is written as a plain name, such as `Point`, and must be matched to a struct declaration?"

    A named type. Name resolution finds the struct declaration it refers to.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#411-type-equality).

??? question "What do you declare to group related values into a new named type, such as `Point` with `x` and `y`?"

    A struct. Declaring it creates a type; a struct expression creates a value of that type.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../specification/structs.md#81-declaration).

??? question "What is one size in an array type such as `[f32; 4, 8]` called, and when must it be known?"

    A dimension. Each one must evaluate at compile time to an integer that fits `usize`.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#72-dimension-rules).

??? question "Which function does every executable Vortex program start running from, and what must it look like in v0.1?"

    The entry point, `main`. In v0.1 it takes no parameters, returns `void`, and there must be exactly one.

    Introduced in [3. Hello world and main](03-hello-world.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#33-entry-point).

??? question "What do we call a name the programmer chose, such as `width` or `Point`?"

    An identifier. It starts with a letter or `_`, continues with letters, digits or `_`, and is case-sensitive.

    Introduced in [2. Basic source rules](02-basic-source-rules.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../specification/lexical-structure.md#23-identifiers).

??? question "What must the operand of `&` or `&mut` be, and why is `a + b` not allowed?"

    Addressable, meaning it names real storage such as a variable, field or array element; `a + b` is only a temporary result.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [9. References and mutability](../specification/references.md#92-reference-expressions).
